proposed_schedule.first_concrete_ask: DTR: do you require the processes on 8191/8193? If they are idle leftovers of either project, whichever owns them stops them and takes no lease, and the host is free for the first project that needs it.
proposed_schedule.principle: the host serves one accelerator consumer at a time, by explicit lease, rather than by whoever started first keeping it indefinitely
rules: a project starts an accelerator process ONLY while holding an unexpired lease
a lease names an expiry; an expired lease is released by its holder, never seized by the other
on release the holder STOPS its own processes -- no project ever stops another project's
a project with no lease runs CPU-only work, which is what both are largely doing now
the lease file is advisory and auditable: it records intent so a blocked project can see who holds the host and until when

status: PROPOSAL. Nothing stopped, started or rescheduled. Awaiting the other project and the owner.
what_I_will_not_do: stop, signal or inspect beyond ps/lsof any process I do not own
seize the host because a lease looks stale
treat this proposal as agreement, or start anything before both the other project and the owner respond
why: Two llama-servers hold ports 8191/8193 on the shared host. ICLR's protocol 5.7.2 fails its quiescence gate on the PRESENCE of a non-baseline accelerator consumer, so their existence alone has kept the live study at ZERO episodes for a full day.
